question: How is BlockSuite, the editor framework under `blocksuite/`, structured: what are its main packages and kinds of components, and how does the AFFiNE app use it?

points.text: BlockSuite has two groups of packages: a headless framework (`blocksuite/framework`: `@blocksuite/store`, `@blocksuite/std` and support packages) and the prebuilt editing components built on it (`blocksuite/affine`: the blocks, widgets, fragments, models and shared code); the framework does not depend on the components
`@blocksuite/store` is the data layer: documents are modeled on the Yjs CRDT, which gives them real-time collaboration and history (undo/redo)

`@blocksuite/std` (the docs' `block-std`) is the standard library for editable blocks: UI event handling, selection and clipboard (with commands), and the `EditorHost` that turns the block tree into components
rich text is handled by a small inline editor (the docs' `@blocksuite/inline`): each block's text is its own Y.Text with its own inline editor, instead of one rich-text editor for the whole document

its component types are editors (the page editor and the edgeless whiteboard editor), blocks, widgets (helper UI that shows up for a block, such as the slash menu or drag handle) and fragments (UI outside the editor that shares its document, such as the doc title or outline panel)
all of these components are native web components built with lit, while the AFFiNE app is written in React, so the app wraps BlockSuite's editors in React components

an editor is thin, just the set of block and widget registrations mounted on an `EditorHost`; so the page and edgeless editors are two views of the same document, and the root block keeps one model (`RootBlockModel`, flavour `affine:page`) with a different view in each
BlockSuite stands apart from the app, like Monaco from VS Code: the app depends on BlockSuite and reuses it through its components, and BlockSuite never imports the app's code

answer:
BlockSuite lives in `blocksuite/` and splits into two layers: a generic `framework/` and an AFFiNE-specific `affine/`. I worked this out from the package layout and the file names under `packages/frontend/core/src/blocksuite/`. I didn't open any source files, so the descriptions below are inferred from names.

**`blocksuite/framework/`: the generic core**
- `global`: shared utilities and base types.
- `store`: the document and block data model. Docs are collaborative and CRDT-backed, and the store handles schema, transactions and extensions.
- `sync`: syncing docs and blobs with storage and other clients.
- `std`: the standard editor runtime. It holds the dependency-injection container, extension system, commands, selection, clipboard, the block and widget view base classes, and the graphics (`gfx`) layer behind edgeless canvas mode.

**`blocksuite/affine/`: the AFFiNE implementation, built on the framework**
- Support packages: `model` (block schemas and models), `shared`, `foundation`, `components` (shared UI), `rich-text`, `data-view`, `ext-loader`, and `all`, which seems to bundle everything.
- `blocks/*`: one package per block type.
  - Text blocks: paragraph, list, code, divider, latex, callout and table.
  - Page structure: note, root and frame.
  - Media and embeds: image, attachment, bookmark, embed and embed-doc.
  - Data and canvas: database, data-view, surface, surface-ref and edgeless-text.
- `gfx/*`: edgeless canvas tools and elements, such as brush, shape, connector, mindmap, group, text and template. `turbo-renderer` is a rendering optimisation.
- `inlines/*`: inline rich-text features such as link, reference, mention, footnote, comment and latex.
- `widgets/*`: UI overlays such as the slash menu, toolbar, drag handle, the edgeless toolbars, remote-selection, linked-doc and note-slicer.
- `fragments/*`: side panels such as outline, frame-panel, doc-title and adapter-panel.

Each package is a self-contained extension, which is the unit the framework's extension system registers. That lets an app compose only the pieces it wants.

**How the AFFiNE app uses it**
- The app, mainly `packages/frontend/core`, imports `@blocksuite/affine/*`, `@blocksuite/std` and `@blocksuite/store`. Imports of those packages appear in over 300 files.
- `packages/frontend/core/src/blocksuite/` is the integration layer:
  - `manager/store.ts` and `manager/view.ts` assemble the store and view extension sets.
  - `view-extensions/*` adds AFFiNE-specific behaviour: cloud, electron, mobile, theme, comments, PDF and database integrations, link previews and editor config.
  - `store-extensions/*` covers feature flags and AI.
  - `editors/page-editor.ts` and `editors/edgeless-editor.ts` define the two editor modes, document and canvas.
  - `block-suite-editor/` wraps the editor for React, with `lit-adaper.tsx` bridging React and Lit.
  - Other folders hold the mode switch, outline viewer, attachment viewer and starter bar.
- `blocksuite/ai/` is a large AI layer. It adds a custom AI chat block, a chat UI and copilot widgets on top of BlockSuite's extension points.
